html.Nejstarší a nejvýznamnější památka Touži: Toužim's oldest and most important historic building. A provostry became a castle, the castle became a château, then decades of decay. Since 2015 it has been coming back to life.
html.Krajinu na horním toku Střely dostává od: The ruler grants the land on the upper reaches of the Střela river to the nobleman Jiří of Milevsko. On the site of the castle he builds a manor, probably named after its first steward, Túžim ("longed-for son").
html.Jiří zakládá premonstrátský klášter v Mi: Jiří founds the Premonstratensian monastery in Milevsko and also bequeaths the Toužim area to it. The Premonstratensians turn the manor into a provostry with the Church of St John the Baptist.
html.Proboštství vyplenili šlechtici bojující: The provostry is plundered by nobles fighting against King Wenceslas IV, and Provost Jiří is taken prisoner.
html.Král Zikmund dává panství do zástavy hus: King Sigismund pledges the estate to the Hussite captain Jakoubek of Vřesovice. With his son Jan he rebuilds the provostry as a Gothic castle, today the core of the Upper Castle (Jan's Castle).
html.Král Jiří z Poděbrad povoluje měšťanům v: King George of Poděbrady allows the townspeople of plundered Útviny to build a new fortified town next to the castle. Toužim is founded.
html.Panství získávají páni z Plavna. Přistav: The estate passes to the Lords of Plauen. They add a late Gothic palace and in the first half of the 16th century rebuild the castle in Renaissance style: the Upper and Lower Castle, a manor farm and a garden with a fountain are created.
The estate is inherited by the Lobkowicz family of Hasištejn.
html.Zámek i město vyhořely. O tři roky pozdě: The castle and town burn down. Three years later Duke Julius Henry of Saxe-Lauenburg buys the estate and rebuilds the castle as an early Baroque residence with a park and a summer house. The Church of St John the Baptist disappears; the Chapel of the Holy Cross stands in its place.
html.Další požár. Při obnově vzniká nový pans: Another fire. During the rebuilding a new manorial brewery is built.
html.Panství dědí bádenská markrabata. Zámek: The estate is inherited by the Margraves of Baden. The castle no longer serves as a noble residence, only for farming and administration.
html.Zámek znovu vyhořel. Dolní zámek dostává: The castle burns down again. The Lower Castle gets its present late Baroque appearance.
html.Panství připadá panovníkovi. Část chátra: The estate passes to the sovereign. Part of the decaying castle is demolished.
html.Horní zámek přichází o celé horní patro: The Upper Castle loses its entire top floor with the tower, and both wings. The garden with the summer house disappears too.
html.Panství kupuje v dražbě vévoda Alfred Be: Duke Alfred Beaufort-Spontin buys the estate at auction. The family keeps it until 1945.
html.Zámek přechází na stát. Využívá ho armád: The castle passes to the state. It is used by the army, a state farm, the district national committee and later the town.
html.Kvůli panelovému sídlišti jsou zbořeny n: Some of the farm buildings are demolished to make way for a prefab housing estate.
html.Obnova, připravovaná od 70. let, se úpln: Restoration, in preparation since the 1970s, comes to a complete halt.
html.Město zámek prodává soukromé osobě. Záme: The town sells the castle to a private owner. It falls into decay and is damaged by vandals.

html.Z rozsáhlého panského sídla se dochovalo: Of the extensive manorial seat, mainly the core has survived: the Upper and Lower Castle, the manorial brewery, the fountain, the Chapel of the Holy Cross and part of the manor farm. Surviving parts are highlighted in yellow in the drawing.

html.Hlavní rezidence. Tvoří ho pozůstatek ob: The main residence. It is built around the remains of the provostry's living quarters, rebuilt as a castle after 1437. On the west and south sides, walls with a round bastion and the entrance gate have survived. The Renaissance rebuilding turned it into a grand château, which was altered again after the fires of 1620, 1652 and 1752. In the early 19th century it lost a whole floor along with its tower.
html.Vznikl renesanční přestavbou gotického p: It was created by the Renaissance rebuilding of the Gothic outer ward and was used to run the estate. After the 17th-century fires it was given a painted beamed ceiling; its present appearance dates from late Baroque alterations after 1752. There was a water cistern in the cellars. The north wing was demolished in the 19th century, leaving only the riding hall. In the courtyard stands the base of a column of St John of Nepomuk from 1800.
html.Panský pivovar stál v zahradě nejpozději: The manorial brewery stood in the garden from 1661 at the latest, and its cellar has survived. The present brewery building is a Baroque new build from after 1752. In front of it stands a stone fountain from the castle garden. The Chapel of the Holy Cross replaced the provostry's Church of St John the Baptist.
html.Byla založena severně od zámku snad už p: It was laid out north of the castle, perhaps as early as before 1620, and greatly enlarged after 1625. A French-style park with ponds, fountains, an orchard, a gardener's house and a Renaissance summer house was enclosed by a stone wall. The garden disappeared in the 19th century and today most of its area is covered by a housing estate.
html.Založen před rokem 1544 severovýchodně o: Founded before 1544 north-east of the castle. Besides farming it also served for defence: the three-winged complex by the town wall formed a massive bastion with loopholes. It included farmhands' quarters, cowsheds, a granary, a barn, stables, a coach house, the steward's house and a dovecote. The Jewish Gate to the ghetto in Předměstí led through the east wing.
html.Dolní neboli Rybářská brána měla v 17. s: In the 17th century the Lower or Fishermen's Gate housed the castle armoury on its upper floor; it was demolished in 1847. The castle pond in the Střela valley was part of the town's defences and disappeared after a flood at the end of the 19th century. The dam with its weir and a stone two-arched bridge survive. The castle mill disappeared after 1960.

html.Kdysi dávno, v době přemyslovských králů: Long ago, in the days of the Přemyslid kings, the monastery estate at Toužim was run by Provost Dluhoš. He was very capable, but also very greedy. He grew rich at the expense of his subjects and of the monastery, and hid the wealth he amassed in the cellars of his house. Word of Dluhoš's deeds reached the abbot himself. He came to Toužim with his fellow canons to question the provost, but Dluhoš would not give up his riches and kept denying what he had done. As punishment he was dressed in a black habit and, as the "black sheep" of the order, walled up in the vaults of the provostry together with his stolen treasure.
html.Z klášterního statku se stal hrad, z hra: The monastery estate became a castle, and the castle a château. Through the centuries the soul of the "black monk" has wandered the underground passages. It will only be set free when someone with a pure heart finds Dluhoš's treasure and gives it to those in need.

html.Horní zámek je nejstarší částí areálu. U: The Upper Castle is the oldest part of the site. It hides the Romanesque-Gothic remains of the provostry, the castle's residential tower and a late Gothic palace that was extended in Renaissance style around 15442. It is named after Jan of Vřesovice, who had a strong castle built here7. At the request of Jan II of Vřesovice, who held the castle in pledge, King George of Poděbrady allowed a new town to be founded next to the castle in 14693.
html.Hrad vznikl po roce 1437 přestavbou obyt: The castle was created after 1437 by rebuilding the residential building of the provostry. On the west and south sides its walls with a round bastion and the entrance gate have survived. The Renaissance rebuild turned it into a grand château, which was altered again after the fires of 1620, 1652 and 1752.
html.Na počátku 19. století, kdy už zámek nes: In the early 19th century, when the castle no longer served the nobility but the estate's farming, the upper floor including the tower was taken down and the south wing was demolished too. Part of the castle then housed the estate offices and flats of Toužim townspeople4. What the Upper Castle looked like before and after the demolition is shown by an oil painting by G. Döbler from around 1800 and a drawing by F. Heber from around 1850.

html.Památkový katalog ho vede jako „Janův zá: The heritage catalogue lists it as “Janův zámek, tzv. Horní hrad” (Jan's Castle, the so-called Upper Castle)5. Beware of confusion: there is also a Jan's Castle near Lednice. That one is several centuries younger; it was begun in 1801 as a hunting lodge of the Liechtenstein family9. If you are looking for the one in Toužim, add “Toužim”.
html.„Nový“ neznamená nedávný. Jméno ho jen o: “New” does not mean recent. The name only distinguishes it from the older Jan's Castle. It was created by a Renaissance rebuild of the Gothic outer bailey. The portal is dated 1544, further alterations followed in 1576–1578 and after the fires of the 17th century2. Its main façade faces the square6.
html.Na dvoře má pilířové arkády, v patře poz: The courtyard has pillared arcades, later walled up on the upper floor. If you look closely, the shape of the arches is still visible in the wall6. The north wing, demolished in the 19th century, once connected the two castles2. Only the riding hall remains of it.
html.Dolní zámek sloužil správě panství. Po p: The Lower Castle served the administration of the estate. After the fires of the 17th century it received a painted beamed ceiling; its present appearance comes from late Baroque alterations after 1752. There was a water cistern in the cellar. In the courtyard stands the base of a column of St John of Nepomuk from 1800.
html.Dvůr Dolního zámku v roce 2015. Zazděné: The courtyard of the Lower Castle in 2015. The walled-up arches on the upper floor are clearly visible.

html.Po válce kasárna, později knihovna, osvě: After the war barracks, later a library, a cultural centre and a furniture shop. Big celebrations of 500 years of the town in 1969.

html.Po válce zámek sloužil armádě jako kasár: After the war the castle served the army as barracks. At the end of the 1960s the building by the square (no. 1) housed the district public library, the cultural centre and the art school, and on the ground floor there was a furniture shop.
html.V červnu 1969 slavila Toužim 500 let od: In June 1969 Toužim celebrated 500 years since its founding. From 8 to 15 June the castle hall hosted an exhibition of the town's heritage. It was prepared by Josef Běhavý to a script by architect Karel Kibic of SÚPPOP Prague. On display were charters and seals from the district archive in Karlovy Vary, Hallstatt and La Tène finds from the Karlovy Vary district museum and a statue of the Madonna from the Toužim deanery.
html.Výstavu zahájil 8. června Aleš Polák za: The exhibition was opened on 8 June by Aleš Polák on behalf of the celebrations committee. People who had left Toužim, he said, would keep “a memory of childhood in a town with an unpretentious castle, a memory of storks flying to their nest on the old chimney of the former brewery”.
The main day of the celebrations was Sunday 15 June. There was an old Czech fair on the sports ground and a match between former internationals of AC Sparta and TJ Toužim. In the afternoon a historical procession of King George of Poděbrady, who granted Toužim its town privileges, passed through the town. The day ended with a performance by Historický šerm Praha.

html.V roce 2011 byly obě zámecké budovy nest: In 2011 both castle buildings were unstable ruins. A strong wind tore off part of the roof of the Upper Castle, and thieves were stealing the copper roofing from the Lower Castle2.
html.V letech 2014 a 2015 zkoumal Mikuláš Tic: In 2014 and 2015 Mikuláš Tichý studied the communities of Toužim, and people kept telling him that the castle was a “black hole” in the middle of the town. He was inspired by the revival of Skoky led by Jiří Schierl. In June 2015 about 60 people came to a community meeting, and work days in the courtyard began that same summer. This initiative gave rise to the Živý zámek Toužim association, registered on 28 January 2016. For ten years it was chaired by Michal Nedvídek; since July 2026 its chair has been Pavla Vokurková.
html.Propadlá střecha Janova hradu, duben 201: The collapsed roof of Jan's Castle, April 2011. Photo Jiří Schierl.
html.Zámek patří městu a nádvoří otvíráme lid: The castle belongs to the town, and we open the courtyard to the public with its consent. The condition was to block the entrances to the dangerous buildings, so at the first work days we built a fence and barriers, cleared the courtyard of self-sown trees and repaired benches and tables. In summer 2016 the courtyard was opened for the first time on weekends with guided tours.
html.Většinu práce odvedli dobrovolníci na br: Most of the work was done by volunteers at work days, with help from the town and donors. At the end of August 2019 we built a roof over the stage in nine days. In 2019 the castle chamber got a new floor and today it has information panels, pictures and lighting. In 2020 we opened the first chamber in the castle.
Jan's Castle in March 2011, before repairs. Photo Jiří Schierl.
html.S městem vzniklo zábradlí na baště nad K: Together with the town we added a railing on the bastion above Karlovarská Street (2021) and toilets with running water (2024). In 2023, painted boards for the broken windows were made with the Information Centre and the primary school.
html.Od jara 2026 zakládáme <a href=\"zahrada: Since spring 2026 we have been creating the castle garden. During the work we came across medieval masonry; more in the section Archaeology at the castle.

html.Opravy budov se zatím týkají hlavně pivo: So far the repairs have mainly concerned the brewery and Jan's Castle. The brewery has a new roof, façades and windows. At Jan's Castle the wall tops were consolidated, the collapsed vaults, the shaft of the spiral staircase and the gables were rebuilt, and the restored roof truss has a temporary sheet-metal roof for now. The Lower Castle is still decaying. It has a temporary roof and structural defects at its corners. That is why the National Heritage Institute lists the site among endangered monuments1.

We photographed them in October 2020, because as the buildings decay further they will probably disappear.

In spring and autumn there is the Castle CITO, a work day with geocachers. Then come Children's Day, the rock Festival at the Castle, the Historical Day marking the anniversary of Toužim becoming a town, the Castle Fair, Punkovice and Theatre at the Castle. html.Při zakládání zámecké zahrady zkoumáme,: While creating the castle garden we are exploring what lies underground. So far we have uncovered two defensive walls of the castle. The survey continues and we will keep adding to this article.
html.V roce 2024 udělal Archeologický ústav A: In 2024 the Institute of Archaeology of the Czech Academy of Sciences carried out a geophysical survey of the courtyard and the brewery.
html.V březnu 2026 jsme pod hlínou narazili n: In March 2026 we came across the original defensive wall under the soil, probably from the early 15th century. In April archaeologists examined and documented it. To keep it protected we will cover it again and put up an information board with photos from the survey next to the find.
html.V říjnu jsme odkryli část horní hradební: In October we uncovered part of the upper defensive wall. It is a different wall from the March find. A piece of the same wall was already uncovered by an archaeological survey in 1974. At the end of October a local historian surveyed it and extended the trench by another section.
html.Historické jádro Toužimi je od roku 1992: The historic centre of Toužim has been a protected heritage zone since 19923. Besides the castle it has the town hall, a fountain, a plague column, the deanery church and burghers' houses, which often have Gothic cellars.
html.Hrad tu byl dřív než město. Toužim vznik: The castle was here before the town. Toužim was founded in 1469 as a new fortified town right next to the castle, and the two fortifications were joined together3.
html.Na jižní a západní straně chránila město: On the south and west sides the town was protected not only by its walls but also by the landscape: a slope and the waterlogged floodplain of the Střela, soon flooded by the Castle Pond. On the opposite sides, open to gently rising ground, there was also an outer wall behind the town wall, with a moat and an earth rampart in front of it. The corners were guarded by bastions or towers3.
html.Do města se vcházelo třemi branami. Horn: The town was entered through three gates. The Upper Gate had the town tower, the Church Gate was tower-like. The most interesting was the Lower Gate by the castle fortifications, similar to the Bechyně Gate in Tábor: it had an upper floor with loopholes and a passage protected by a barbican3.
html.Od západu, odkud přišla zkáza Útviny, se: From the west, where the destruction of Útvina had come from, the way led along the top of the Castle Pond dam. The path turned on it, was interrupted by a narrow bridge over the weir and then led back along the bank to the gate. Anyone approaching was within range of the loopholes of both the castle and the Lower Gate the whole time3.
html.Toužim na císařském otisku stabilního ka: Toužim on the imperial copy of the stable cadastre from 1841. The castle site is on the left above the Castle Pond (Schloß Teich), next to it the Castle Mill (Schloß Mühle). Central Archive of Surveying and Cadastre23.
html.Toužim z letadla, 16. 10. 2017. Uprostře: Toužim from the air, 16 October 2017. The square in the middle, the castle to the left below it. Photo Jiří Schierl.
html.Co zbylo z hradeb a bran: What is left of the walls and gates
html.Dolní bráně se říkalo také Rybářská nebo: The Lower Gate was also called the Fishermen's or Loket Gate, the Upper Gate the Plzeň Gate. A fourth, small Jewish or Court Gate led through the manor farm to the northern suburb16.
html.Zámek od Zámeckého rybníka, kresba A. Le: The castle from the Castle Pond, drawing by A. Lewy in the book Čechy, 1896. On the left the two-arched bridge on the dam.
html.Žádná z bran se nedochovala. Rybářskou a: None of the gates has survived. The Fishermen's and Upper Gates were demolished after the town fire of 1847 because they were in the way of the new imperial road from Plzeň to Loket. The Church Gate lost its upper floor in the same fire. Its new half-timbered floor then served as a synagogue, and when there was another fire in 1872 the whole gate was demolished. The Jewish Gate disappeared with the clearance of the manor farm in the 1960s16.
html.Z hradeb zůstal souvislý pás na západní: Of the walls, a continuous stretch remains on the west and south sides of the town, in places up to five metres high. Today they often hold up gardens and yards or serve as foundations of houses. Other pieces stand behind the church, in the yards of houses no. 56 to 58 and in the gardens on the north side of the square. In Karlovarská Street by no. 344 the remains of the foundations of the Fishermen's Gate can be seen. The old name of part of Pod Brankou Street, Na Příkopu (On the Moat), still recalls the moat16.
html.Náměstí: radnice, kašna a morový sloup: The square: town hall, fountain and plague column
html.<b>Radnice čp. 35</b> je pozdně gotická,: The town hall, no. 35, is late Gothic, probably from the second half of the 15th century17. After the fires of 1620, 1652, 1752 and 1872 it was rebuilt each time. The stone plaque with the coat of arms above the entrance survives from a portal from the period after 1500. On the ground floor there are vaulted halls and a black kitchen. In the cellar a dungeon has survived and, rarely, also a remnant of the wooden formwork on which the vault was built. In 2004 the town hall got back its Classicist-Empire appearance2,17.
html.<b>Kašnu na náměstí</b> napájel městský: The fountain on the square was fed by the town water supply through wooden pipes from the Pipe Pond2. The granite basin measures about 3.9 × 3.9 metres. Originally a column with two round bowls stood in the middle. Around 1930 it was replaced by today's three-metre sandstone pylon by local sculptor Karl Fuchs. It is decorated with round reliefs of flowers, and water flows from openings in two of them2,20.
html.<b>Morový sloup</b> se sochou Panny Mari: The plague column with a statue of the Virgin Mary dates from 1705; the year is carved on the pedestal. The Virgin wears a crown and holds a sceptre, and on her right arm she holds the Infant Jesus with an apple topped by a gilded cross. The capital of the column is decorated with winged heads of cherubs19. The statues of Saints Joseph, Florian, John of Nepomuk and John the Baptist at the corners are probably somewhat younger. Lanterns once hung on the iron brackets of the pedestals2.
html.Kostel Narození Panny Marie: Church of the Nativity of the Virgin Mary
html.Kostel založili asi po roce 1488. Z goti: The church was founded probably after 1488. Of the Gothic building, the north tower remains. In 1738–1742 it was rebuilt in Baroque style by builder Johann Schmied of Útvina, and after the fires of 1774–1778 and 1872 it was restored again. Inside are wall paintings by J. J. Kramolín from 1778: a painted high altar and two side altars2. The north Ecce Homo chapel was built as early as 1699 by J. Socka; the south chapel was added to a design by H. A. Biedtermann18.
html.K areálu kostela patří ohradní zeď se dv: The church grounds include an enclosing wall with two gates18. Next to it stand the old rectory no. 64/65, the school no. 8 and the former mortuary, today the Mount of Olives chapel2. The deanery no. 19 was built in Baroque style in the same years as the church, on the site of the medieval rectory12.
html.Měšťanské domy a starý pivovar: Burghers' houses and the old brewery
html.<b>Steinbachův dům čp. 51</b> stojí v Pl: The Steinbach House, no. 51, stands in Plzeňská Street, which led from the square to the Upper Gate. It has a late Gothic stone core. It is named after Anton Steinbach of Kranichstein, chief steward of the Saxe-Lauenburg estates, who owned it in the second half of the 17th century. An older charter calls it “the Big Green One” or “the Big Green”. After the fires of 1485, 1620, 1652, 1752 and 1847 it was rebuilt each time. Its Renaissance portal with a coat of arms, Steinbach's monogram and the year 1657 was taken to Bečov Castle in 1907 and to Loket Castle in 192710.
html.Nárožní <b>panský dům čp. 53</b> v téže: The corner manor house, no. 53, in the same street already stood before 1661. After the fire of 1847 it became a house for estate officials. At that time a clock and a heraldic plaque from 1661 with the arms of Duke Julius Henry of Saxony and his wife Anna Magdalena of Lobkowicz were moved to its façade from the demolished Upper Gate. The clockwork was destroyed when the house burned in 1896; the coat of arms was restored in 200411,16.
html.<b>Dům čp. 43</b> na náměstí má kamenný: House no. 43 on the square has a stone Renaissance portal that was moved here from house no. 50 in 1907. The keystone bears the year 1600, the monogram G.S.S. and the sign of the maltsters' guild with hop leaves2,22.
html.<b>Dům čp. 58</b> si jako jediný v Touži: House no. 58 is the only one in Toužim to have kept the original layout of a wide burgher's house: an entrance hall, a hall with a small Renaissance portal and a black kitchen2.
html.<b>Domy čp. 56 a 57</b> mají gotický skl: Houses no. 56 and 57 have a Gothic cellar and on the ground floor a hall with a Renaissance groin vault with ridges. House no. 98, once part of the town hall, has a Renaissance vault on the ground floor2.
html.V bývalém panském zájezdním hostinci <b>: In the former manorial coaching inn no. 7 three wall paintings from 1932 remain, showing old Toužim and the town of that time. When house no. 102 was demolished, stone paving, the foundations of an oven and ceramics and glass from the 16th to 18th centuries were found2.
html.<b>Starý obecní pivovar čp. 69</b> má po: The old municipal brewery, no. 69, has extensive underground brewery cellars with 15th-century water cisterns2.
html.Druhá toužimská <b>kašna</b> stojí v are: Toužim's second fountain stands in the castle grounds, in the former castle garden in front of the brewery, between four trees. It is shown in the same place on the 1841 map, and a plan of the castle brewery from the second half of the 17th century already has a square fountain. The stone in the middle bears traces of a part that has not survived21.
html.Pod zámkem se dochoval zbytek <b>barokní: Below the castle the remains of a 17th-century Baroque stone bridge with two vaulted arches survive. Today it serves as the cellar of the neighbouring garden14.
html.<b>Kaplička svaté Anny</b>, německy Radi: St Anne's Chapel, in German Radinger-Kapelle, is a small 18th-century Baroque building only about 2.5 metres wide. Its vault inside is painted as a night sky with stars, and under the plaster hides the inscription “Renoviert 1922”15.
html.Na Plzeňském předměstí stojí <b>škola čp: In the Plzeň suburb stands the school no. 330 from 1923 by Karlovy Vary architect Karl Ernstberger, a pupil of Otto Wagner. Each side of the building has a different façade. The niches hold reliefs of children learning, and the east gable has figures of a man and a woman representing education and wisdom. The decoration was probably made by Willi Russ of Krásno. The building is still a school today13.
html.Tři příběhy: o chamtivém proboštovi Dluh: Three stories: about the greedy Provost Dluhoš, who wanders the underground as the Black Monk, and about two terrifying guests in the castle hall.
html.Pověst o chamtivém proboštovi Dluhošovi: The legend of the greedy Provost Dluhoš as a comic. Our association had it drawn for the castle; the artist is West Bohemian illustrator Dalibor Nesnídal. It is based on a fictional account by the aged Premonstratensian Fr Josef Bartoloměj Nikl. Tap a page to enlarge it.
html.Na plese na zámku odmítla dáma opilého p: At a ball at the castle a lady turned down a drunken gentleman with the words: “I would rather dance with the devil!” Then an unknown guest danced with her and left shortly after midnight. Only then did everyone notice that instead of one foot he had a hoof8.
html.Po půlnoci se v zámeckém sále objevila d: After midnight a terrifying figure appeared in the castle hall and stamped its hooves on the floor. The guests fled and the parquet gave way. What really happened there is not known. The legend was written down by Josef Russ in 1936 under the title “Der Gottseibeiuns im Schlosse zu Theussing”8.

html.Město pojmenované po hradu: A town named after the castle
html.Když král v roce 1469 dovolil měšťanům z: When the king allowed the townspeople of Útvina to build a new town in 1469, it was named after the castle: Toužim.
html.Znak po Útvině: A coat of arms from Útvina
html.Nová Toužim převzala práva vypálené Útvi: The new Toužim took over the rights of burnt-down Útvina and its town coat of arms. It received a new coat of arms in 1478.
html.Toužim se stavěla „na zeleném drnu“. Pro: Toužim was built on a greenfield site. That is why it has right-angled streets and a square slightly off-centre.
html.V opačném rohu města než hrad stál farní: In the opposite corner of the town from the castle stood the parish church with a defensive tower.
html.Tolik v roce 1837 zaplatil v dražbě vévo: That is what Duke Alfred Beaufort-Spontin, a Belgian nobleman who had come to Bohemia fleeing Napoleon, paid at auction in 1837.
html.V 19. století byl zámecký pivovar spolu: In the 19th century the castle brewery, together with a brickworks and a sawmill, was the only “industrial” enterprise in the town. It was modernised in 1901.
html.Malovaný trámový strop Dolního zámku je: The painted beamed ceiling of the Lower Castle is stored outside the site for its protection.
html.Hospodářské budovy zámku jsou v podstatě: The castle's farm buildings are essentially Baroque; in the 19th century they were only altered.
html.Antonín Steinbach (1615–1674) za třiceti: Anton Steinbach (1615–1674) managed the Toužim estate during the Thirty Years' War and grew rich. He bought Líšťany and in 1664 became a knight “of Kranichstein”. House no. 51 recalls him. More about him: Líšťany municipality (in Czech), Wikipedia (in German).
The first locomotive arrived in Toužim on 14 June 1898 by road, on a wagon pulled by eight pairs of horses. To have the railway run through the town, the people of Toužim contributed 200,000 guilders.
html.Vařit se v pivovaru přestalo brzy po prv: Brewing stopped soon after the First World War. After that beer was only bottled here, until the end of the Second World War, when the brewery burned down.

html.Průzkumy na zámku našly barokní krov. Je: Surveys at the castle found a Baroque roof truss. It is the oldest surviving roof truss in Toužim.
